1	# Agent Note: The read barrier as filesystem and process authority
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-05-read-barrier.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	A certificate proves only what the implementer could not reach, and nothing in the repository decides that. [`dsh-verification`](../../../../packages/verification/verification/README.md) commits a `verification/certificate` only for a fully passing run and stamps it with a `CertificateIsolation` of `none`, `process`, or `host`, but its own Known Limitations name the missing read barrier: the standard's `run` instructions are readable by any in-process consumer of the log, and denying implementer reads is filesystem-policy work in a plugin that does not exist.
10	
11	The implementer and the checks share one filesystem and one operating-system user. `EnvironmentRunner.run()` creates the implementer's agent with `meta.cwd = workspace` and then executes every check through `ctx.shell` with `workdir: workspace` from the same process ([`packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts`](../../../../packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts)); its README states that the read barrier is the deployment's. The standard is in the implementer's own session log, which [`dsh-session-persistence-jsonl`](../../../../packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/README.md) keeps as ordinary files under its configured root. [`dsh-credentials-local`](../../../../packages/credentials/credentials-local/README.md) already records what that costs: owner-only modes stop other operating-system users and not the model, because tool processes run as the same user and the shipped file policy confines mutations rather than reads.
12	
13	Composition decides what an implementer can read, and no composition is checked. A preset that mounts [`dsh-tool-session-query`](../../../../packages/session-query/tool-session-query/README.md) hands the model five tools that read the durable session log; one that mounts [`dsh-tool-cordis`](../../../../packages/extensions/tool-cordis/README.md) lets it define and mount a plugin into the live process. `tools.restrict()` and subagent `toolFilter` are visibility composition per [agent-scope-contexts](../../implemented/architecture/2026-07-08-agent-scope-contexts.md), not authority, and a certificate carries no durable record of which tools its session composed.
14	
15	An isolation claim above `none` therefore has no evidence behind it. `recordRun()` writes the level its caller passes; the invariant companion validates revisions, append-only check growth, and certificate coverage, and never asks what the level asserts. Keeping only `process` and `host` runs — the reward-gaming mitigation the [trajectory-export note](2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md) names, and the column the [fleet leaderboard](../../../../packages/improvement/fleet/README.md) refuses to average across — filters on an unchecked field.
16	
17	Nothing detects a workspace the implementer edited underneath its own checks. A task whose fixture supplies the tests it will be graded on is graded on whatever those files say at validation time, and the runner compares nothing between the overlay it wrote and the tree it measures.
18	
19	## Proposal
20	
21	Make the barrier authority at the executor: one policy owner, per-capability denial where each capability opens paths, and a certificate that may claim only what the composition recorded.
22	
23	**A validator-owned root.** Add `@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier` (`ctx.readBarrier`) at `packages/verification/read-barrier/`: the policy home for denied reads, in the role [`dsh-sandbox-policy`](../../../../packages/sandbox/sandbox-policy/README.md) plays for sandbox mode and workspace root. Its `root` config defaults to `dshHomePath('verification')` through [`dsh-home-paths`](../../../../packages/util/home-paths/README.md) and accepts any absolute or `~`-prefixed directory; the service creates it owner-only (`0700`) at construction and fails loud when it exists with wider modes. `reserve(agent)` mints `<root>/runs/<sessionId>/` for one run and returns its absolute path; the environment runner calls it before appending the `environment/run` stamp and writes there the standard snapshot, one script per check at `checks/<checkId>`, and any fixture the environment marks held out, then resolves each check's `run` against that directory so the command line the implementer can observe in a process listing names a file whose content it cannot read. `protect(path)` registers one more denied directory and returns its disposer, so `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` contributes its session-store root as an effect instead of a deployment repeating it in configuration; `denyRoots` remains a config field for directories no plugin owns. `resolve({ session? })` answers one `ReadBarrierPolicy { role, root, denied, enforcement }`, and `denies(policy, target)` decides containment.
24	
25	**The deny rule.** For a session whose role is `implementer`, a read is denied when the target's canonical path is a denied directory or a descendant of one. Containment is decided the way [`dsh-fs-sandbox`](../../implemented/feature/2026-07-14-cross-family-fs-sandbox.md) decides it: canonicalize first, then test identity or descent through `ctx.fs.contains(parent, child)` on resolved targets, so the policy parses no path strings and an ancestor symlink swapped since resolution is caught by re-canonicalizing immediately before the decision. A target whose containment cannot be decided is denied. Roles `validator` and `unrestricted` are denied nothing; `unrestricted` is the default and leaves every shipped preset exactly as it is today.
26	
27	**The fs policy plugin.** Add `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier` at `packages/fs/fs-read-barrier/`, the read half of the policy layer [`dsh-fs-observation-policy`](../../../../packages/fs/fs-observation-policy/README.md) occupies for writes and edits. It registers no service and takes no config: it injects `readBarrier` and decides one new event. [`dsh-fs`](../../../../packages/fs/fs/README.md) declares `fs/read-intent(target, actor, next)` beside `fs/write-intent` and `fs/edit-intent`, as a `@mode waterfall` returning `FsReadDenial { code: FsErrorCode; message: string } | undefined`; unlike the two single-slot intents this one delegates, because a barrier that owned the slot would stop every later read policy from deciding. The plugin returns a denial for a contained target and calls `next()` otherwise. `FsErrorCode` gains `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED`. `dsh-tool-fs` dispatches the event inside `resolveRegularReadTarget` before `ctx.fs.stat`, so a denied path never reveals presence or absence, and `dsh-tool-str-replace-editor` dispatches it on the `view` command. The tool layer adds no recovery instruction, because no retry of the same call succeeds; the model sees the policy's message verbatim.
28	
29	##### Exact error
30	
31	```markdown
32	read denied: "<path>" is validator-owned — it is not part of this task; continue without it
33	```
34	
35	**What a denial records.** The barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/denied` session event per refusal, carrying `{ version, role, capability, displayPath, root }`, where `capability` names the seam that refused (`fs`, `shell`, `subprocess`, `terminal`). The path is already in the log inside the model's own `tool/call` arguments, so the event adds evidence and no new disclosure. It is a `SessionEventMap` member with `ignorable: true`, so a build that does not know the type still reads the log under the [version mechanism](../../implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md).
36	
37	**Tool authority and the composition-time guard.** `ToolDefinition` in [`dsh-tools`](../../../../packages/core/tools/README.md) gains `authority?: readonly ToolAuthority[]`, never model-visible, where `ToolAuthority` is a merge-extensible union declared by `dsh-tools` with three members at the start: `session-log` (the tool reads durable session events), `plugin-mount` (it mounts or evaluates code in the live runtime), and `runtime-introspection` (it reports the live composition). `dsh-tool-session-query` declares `session-log` on all five of its tools; `dsh-tool-cordis` declares `plugin-mount` on `cordis_define`, `cordis_run`, `cordis_stop`, and `cordis_undefine`, and `runtime-introspection` on `cordis_inspect`. An `implementer` session may compose none of the three. Declaring authority at the tool, rather than a name list at the barrier, means a tool added later is covered by its own declaration.
38	
39	**How a preset declares its role.** A preset's optional `preset.yml` gains `role: implementer | validator | unrestricted`, absent meaning `unrestricted`. It is the one authority claim that file carries, so [`dsh-agent-presets`](../../../../packages/preset/agent-presets/README.md) refuses `validator` from a `user`-trust preset and lists that preset as `broken` with the reason: a locally authored preset that could name itself `validator` would grant itself reads. This is the roster's first enforcing use of `trust`, and its README changes with it. `mountPreset` audits the role after `handle.await()` settles the subtree, beside `inactiveRows`, and rejects the mount when the declared role is `implementer` and any tool in the preset's scope layer declares a denied authority. Because the audit runs inside the agent factory's `setup`, a rejected composition rolls the whole session creation back, so the failure is loud and nothing half-composed survives.
40	
41	##### Exact mount refusal
42	
43	```markdown
44	agent-presets: preset "<id>" declares role "implementer" but composes "<tool>", which carries the "<authority>" authority
45	```
46	
47	**The runtime guard.** The barrier also registers one `ctx.tools.guard()` through the agent's own context at session setup, denying any execution whose definition carries a denied authority for that session's role. Guards run after every `tools/pre-execute` listener and are monotonic, so no later listener can turn the denial back into permission ([`ToolGuard`](../../../../packages/core/tools/src/index.ts)). The mount audit covers the preset's composition; the guard covers a tool registered into the agent's own layer afterwards, including one a subagent driver contributes.
48	
49	##### Exact guard denial
50	
51	```markdown
52	"<tool>" carries the "<authority>" authority and is not callable in an implementer session
53	```
54	
55	**Process-level denial.** The [sandbox seam](../../implemented/feature/2026-07-06-sandbox.md) expresses file effects only, which is why a confined subprocess can still read anything it reaches. `SandboxPolicy` and `SandboxExecutionPolicy` gain `deniedReadRoots: readonly string[]`; `ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve()` fills it from `ctx.readBarrier.resolve({ session })`, so the fs fence and every process runner keep taking one owner-resolved policy per call. `dsh-sandbox-local` implements it per backend — a `bwrap` `--tmpfs` over each root, a Landlock ruleset that omits read access for them, a Seatbelt `(deny file-read* (subpath …))` clause, and the Windows ACL runner's equivalent deny entry — and reports `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` when the selected backend cannot express the denial, so the claim fails rather than the barrier. [`dsh-bash-sandbox`](../../../../packages/shell/bash-sandbox/README.md), `dsh-pwsh-sandbox`, and [`dsh-terminal-bash`](../../../../packages/terminal/terminal-bash/README.md) inherit it without changes. [`dsh-tool-fs-search`](../../../../packages/fs/tool-fs-search/README.md) spawns ripgrep unconfined through `ctx.subprocess` today; it confines that spawn through `ctx.sandbox.confine()` whenever a barrier is in force, and additionally the barrier's tool guard denies a `glob` or `grep` whose `path` argument names a denied root directly.
56	
57	**Executors the barrier cannot confine.** Two composed capabilities open paths the harness cannot fence in-process. [`dsh-workflow-worker-thread`](../../../../packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/README.md) states that its worker is not a security sandbox and that an escaped script recovers Node capabilities with the host process's privileges. The out-of-process [subagent](../../../../packages/subagent/subagent/README.md) providers — `subagent-acp`, `subagent-claude-code`, `subagent-codex`, `subagent-dsh-sdk` — launch a foreign agent with its own tool stack and no harness policy. For an `implementer` session, both refuse to start under a claim of `process` or `host` and record `unenforced` under a claim of `none`. The in-process subagent drivers need no exception: a child joins its parent's standing composition through `composeFrom()`, so it inherits the same census, the same scope layer, and the same role.
58	
59	**The scope census.** Before the session's first `request/header`, the barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/scope` event carrying `{ version, role, presetId, root, denied, census, enforcement }`. `census` is one entry per tool visible to the agent, `{ name, authority }`, which makes the composition's authority durable rather than composition-time-only; the invariant cross-checks it against the tool names in each `request/header`'s assembled schemas, so a tool added after the census is caught. `enforcement` is one entry per path-opening capability the composition registered — `fs`, `shell`, `subprocess`, `terminal`, `subagent`, `workflow` — valued `denied-at-executor`, `unenforced`, or `not-composed`.
60	
61	**The certificate invariant.** `recordRun()` reads `ctx.get('readBarrier')` and refuses to commit a certificate whose isolation exceeds what the session recorded, with `VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN`; the [`./invariant`](../../../../packages/verification/verification/README.md) companion applies the identical rule to the durable stream, so a forged certificate fails replay wherever the companion is installed. Independently of level, both refuse a certificate on a session whose scope census carries a denied authority: composing a log-reading tool forfeits the certificate even when the guard was somehow bypassed. `CertificateIsolation`'s JSDoc changes with the rule: `process` means what the ladder below states rather than in-process read policy alone.
62	
63	**The `host` marker.** `host` is accepted only from a `read-barrier/attestation` event the barrier wrote after verifying a file at the configured `hostAttestation` path: it must exist, be owned by a uid other than the harness process's effective uid, be unwritable by that uid and its groups, and contain exactly the run's environment content hashes as the `environment/run` stamp carries them. An in-process component cannot produce that file without already holding another account's privileges, which is the property the level asserts. On Windows the ownership and write tests read the ACL through the primitives `dsh-sandbox-windows-acl` already owns. Absent or unverifiable, the barrier records no attestation and the claim is refused.
64	
65	**Tamper on check-owned paths.** Check-owned paths are the barrier's denied directories plus the workspace paths an environment declares immutable: `EnvironmentDefinition.task` gains `immutable?: readonly string[]`, workspace-relative paths the fixture supplies and the implementer must not author — the tests, the reference outputs, and any overlaid check script. The runner already hashes a directory in `hashDirectory`; it records the digest of the check-owned set immediately after the fixture overlay and before the implementer's first turn, and again at each validation. The `verification/run` event that the [environment-runner note's second slice](2026-09-05-environment-runner.md) adds carries the attempt's `treeHash`; this note adds `verdict: 'pass' | 'fail' | 'tampered'`. A digest that differs from the baseline is `tampered`: the runner records the run, issues one directive naming tamper without naming a path, stops the attempt loop because the workspace no longer measures the task, and never calls a path that could certify. `foldTrajectory` gains reward basis `tamper` with `outcome: 0`, which outranks any certificate in the same log, and the invariant companion rejects a certificate that follows a `tampered` run.
66	
67	**A blind judge under one licence.** Cross-provider routing is the first answer to a judge whose label affects it, and a deployment with one model licence cannot take it. The second route is filesystem and process isolation plus a judge session that holds no implementer context, which means all of the following and nothing weaker. The judge session is created through `ctx.agents.create` with a fresh `SessionId`, no `parentSessionId`, and no resume or fork seed, so its log begins at its own creation. Its `meta.cwd` is a judge workspace holding a copy of the implementer's tree at the audited attempt's `treeHash`, never the implementer's workspace. Its derived history contains exactly the judge preset's system prompt, the environment's task prompt, and one user message carrying the evidence the auditor chose; no `assistant/message`, `tool/result`, or `verification/directive` from the audited session reaches it. Its preset is `system`-trust and declares `role: validator`, so the composition-time guard still denies it a log-reading tool: a judge that could read the audited log would reconstruct the implementer's reasoning and lose the independence this arrangement provides. The barrier appends a `judge/session` event naming the audited session id and asserting the empty lineage, and the invariant rejects a verdict from a session whose header carries a parent or a seed.
68	
69	## The isolation ladder
70	
71	| Level | What it asserts | Required enforcement | Durable evidence |
72	|---|---|---|---|
73	| `none` | Nothing. Implementer and validator share a filesystem. | None. | The certificate alone; a scope event when the barrier is composed. |
74	| `process` | No executor of the implementer's session opens a denied path. | Every composed path-opening capability records `denied-at-executor`; the session's sandbox mode is `workspace-write` or narrower; workflow workers and out-of-process subagent providers refuse to start. | A `read-barrier/scope` event before the first `request/header`, with role `implementer`, an empty denied-authority intersection, and no `unenforced` entry. |
75	| `host` | The checks and fixtures are outside the harness account's write reach. | Everything `process` requires. | Everything `process` requires plus a `read-barrier/attestation` event the barrier verified from a file the harness process cannot write. |
76	
77	## Alternatives considered
78	
79	**Omit the tools and trust the prompt.** Schema omission and instruction are not enforcement when another caller reaches the same operation, which is why the packages standard requires the decision in the operation that makes it. The barrier denies at the executor and the acceptance criteria test denial there.
80	
81	**Deny reads through `SandboxMode` instead of a separate policy.** `SandboxMode` is a three-value file-effect vocabulary shared by every enforcing family; a fourth value meaning "and cannot read these paths" would make one enum carry two independent decisions, and every consumer that switches on the mode would have to learn the second. `deniedReadRoots` rides the same per-call policy without changing what a mode means.
82	
83	**Subclass the filesystem provider the way `fs-sandbox` does.** One provider registers `ctx.fs` per context and `SandboxedFileSystem` already extends `LocalFileSystem`, so a second fence by inheritance would force a mixin or a fixed provider ladder. The `fs/*` event gate is the layer built for adding policy without a service dependency, and it degrades to the bare provider when the plugin is absent.
84	
85	**Name the forbidden tools in the barrier's config.** A name list is stale the moment a package adds a log-reading tool, and a deployment could shorten it. Authority declared at the tool is carried by the tool, and the denied set for a role is a security invariant rather than a tunable.
86	
87	**Derive the role from the session creator instead of the preset.** The creator knows the intent; only the composition knows what was actually mounted, and the failure this prevents is a preset that composes a tool its role forbids. The preset declares the role, the mount audit checks the composition against it, and the creator's request is refused when the resolved preset's role does not match.
88	
89	**Infer `host` from configuration.** The environment runner already rejected inferred isolation for the same reason: nothing in-process can observe the deployment's arrangement, so an inferred value either devalues an isolated run or lies about a local one. A file another account owns is the smallest fact that cannot be produced from inside the process.
90	
91	**Score tamper as a failing check.** A failed check means the work is incomplete; a modified test means the measurement is void. Folding them would let a trajectory earn partial credit for a workspace whose checks no longer describe the task, so tamper is its own verdict and its own reward basis.
92	
93	**Give the judge the implementer's transcript for context.** A judge that reads the audited reasoning inherits its framing, and the same-lineage mislabeling the [seams note](2026-08-29-verification-improvement-oversight-seams.md) records is what the blind session exists to avoid. The judge receives the task, the tree, and the evidence the auditor selected.
94	
95	## Acceptance criteria
96	
97	- In a Loader-booted composition over `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier/`, a `read` of a file under the barrier root from an `implementer`-role session fails with `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED` and the exact message above, one `read-barrier/denied` event is appended, and the same call from a `validator`-role session in the same process returns the file's content.
98	- The denial is proved through the executor, not the schema: the implementer's `read` tool is registered and visible, and a direct `ctx.fs.readText` from a trusted plugin still succeeds, which the test asserts so the threat model stays explicit.
99	- Mounting the preset at `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier-guard/`, which declares `role: implementer` and composes `dsh-tool-session-query`, rejects with the exact mount refusal and leaves no session behind; a `user`-trust preset declaring `role: validator` is listed `broken` with its reason.
100	- `recordRun()` with `isolation: 'host'` on a session with no verified attestation refuses with `VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN` and commits no certificate; the invariant companion rejects a hand-authored log carrying that certificate at the certificate record.
101	- `recordRun()` with `isolation: 'process'` on a session whose scope event records any `unenforced` capability refuses the same way, and succeeds once every composed capability records `denied-at-executor`.
102	- Over `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier-tamper/`, whose environment marks its test file immutable and whose scripted model overwrites it, the attempt's `verification/run` carries `verdict: 'tampered'`, no certificate exists, the goal stays out of `complete`, and the exported trajectory line has `outcome: 0` with basis `tamper`.
103	- A judge session created for an audited session has no `parentSessionId` and no seed, its derived history holds exactly the judge system prompt, the task prompt, and the evidence message, and the invariant rejects a verdict from a session that carries either.
104	- Two keyless snapshots record what the model sees: `examples/headless-agent/tests/snapshots/read-barrier-denied/` pins the denial text in the transcript and the session log, and `examples/headless-agent/tests/snapshots/read-barrier-tamper/` pins the tamper directive's `<validation_failed>` follow-up. Both replay on macOS and Linux per the [testing policy](../../../../docs/testing.md).
105	
106	## Rollout
107	
108	Each slice lands with its own tests and leaves the gates green on its own.
109	
110	1. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier` with the root, `reserve`, `protect`, `resolve`, `denies`, the `read-barrier/scope` and `read-barrier/denied` events, and its invariant companion. Enforcement records `unenforced` everywhere; nothing is denied yet, and no existing composition changes behavior.
111	2. `fs/read-intent` in `dsh-fs`, `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED`, the dispatches in `dsh-tool-fs` and `dsh-tool-str-replace-editor`, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier`. Adds the `read-barrier` fixture and the `read-barrier-denied` snapshot.
112	3. `ToolAuthority` on `ToolDefinition`, the declarations in `dsh-tool-session-query` and `dsh-tool-cordis`, `role` in `preset.yml`, the `mountPreset` audit, and the per-agent tool guard. Adds the `read-barrier-guard` fixture.
113	4. The certificate invariant: the `recordRun` precondition, the companion's rule, the `read-barrier/attestation` event and its file check, and the `CertificateIsolation` documentation change. The environment runner gains `EnvironmentRunRequest.preset` and refuses a claim above `none` when the resolved preset's role is not `implementer`.
114	5. `deniedReadRoots` on `SandboxPolicy` and `SandboxExecutionPolicy`, the `dsh-sandbox-local` backends, the `dsh-sandbox-policy` fill from the barrier, the confined ripgrep spawn in `dsh-tool-fs-search`, and the refusals in the workflow engine and the out-of-process subagent providers. This is the slice that makes `process` claimable.
115	6. Tamper: `task.immutable` in `dsh-environments`, the runner's baseline and per-attempt digest over check-owned paths, `verdict` on `verification/run`, the `tamper` reward basis in `dsh-trajectories`, and the `read-barrier-tamper` fixture and snapshot. It follows the `verification/run` event from the [environment-runner note's second slice](2026-09-05-environment-runner.md).
116	7. The blind judge: the shipped `system`-trust judge preset, the lineage-free creation path, the `judge/session` event, and the invariant that rejects a seeded judge. The judging Consumer itself belongs to the oversight seam of the [seams note](2026-08-29-verification-improvement-oversight-seams.md).
117	
118	## Risks
119	
120	The barrier is trusted code in the implementer's own process below `host`. A plugin with direct `Session` or `ctx.fs` access appends counterfeit events and reads any path, exactly as `dsh-verification` already states for its durable records. The ladder is honest about this: `none` claims nothing, `process` claims only that the composed executors deny, and `host` is the only level whose evidence comes from outside the process.
121	
122	`process` costs enforcement a deployment may not want. Confining every ripgrep spawn, refusing workflow workers, and refusing out-of-process subagent providers removes capability from implementer sessions that claim it; a deployment that wants those capabilities runs at `none` and keeps a certificate that says so.
123	
124	A check's command line stays observable. The barrier protects the script's content and the fixtures, not the argv a process listing shows, so an environment whose check name or arguments encode the assertion leaks it. Environment authors keep the assertion in the script.
125	
126	The census is only as complete as the composition it was taken from. It is appended before the first request and cross-checked against each `request/header`'s tool names, which catches a tool added later but not a plugin that reads paths without registering a tool at all.
127	
128	Tamper detection is a digest comparison, so it reports that the check-owned set changed and never who changed it or how. A legitimate build step that rewrites a file inside the immutable set fails the run; environment authors declare the immutable set narrowly, and a false verdict costs one run rather than a wrong certificate.
129	
130	Making `trust` enforcing for one field changes what the roster promises. A deployment that configured a `user` root expecting presets to be ordinary compositions now finds one class of declaration refused there; the refusal is listed as a `broken` reason on the same roster page that offers to delete it.
131

.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-read-barrier.md:65:**Executors the barrier cannot confine.** Two composed capabilities open paths the harness cannot fence in-process. [`dsh-workflow-worker-thread`](../../../../packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/README.md) states that its worker is not a security sandbox and that an escaped script recovers Node capabilities with the host process's privileges. The out-of-process [subagent](../../../../packages/subagent/subagent/README.md) providers — `subagent-acp`, `subagent-claude-code`, `subagent-codex`, `subagent-dsh-sdk` — launch a foreign agent with its own tool stack and no harness policy. For an `implementer` session, both refuse to start under a claim of `process` or `host` and record `unenforced` under a claim of `none`. The in-process subagent drivers need no exception: a child joins its parent's standing composition through `composeFrom()`, so it inherits the same census, the same scope layer, and the same role.

## Result

### Decisions (15 lines)

1. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier` (`ctx.readBarrier`, `packages/verification/read-barrier/`) is the policy home, in the role `dsh-sandbox-policy` plays for mode and workspace root; `root` defaults to `dshHomePath('verification')`, created `0700`.
2. `reserve(agent)` mints `<root>/runs/<sessionId>/` holding the standard snapshot, one script per check at `checks/<checkId>`, and held-out fixtures; the runner resolves each `check.run` there, so the argv names a file whose content is unreadable.
3. `protect(path)` lets `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` register its session-store root as an effect, closing the "read your own log" hole; `denyRoots` config covers directories no plugin owns.
4. Deny rule: role `implementer` + canonical path identical to or descended from a denied directory, decided through `ctx.fs.contains` after re-canonicalization, fail-closed when undecidable; `validator`/`unrestricted` unaffected, `unrestricted` the default so no shipped preset changes.
5. `dsh-fs` gains `fs/read-intent` as a delegating waterfall (not single-slot, so later read policies still decide); `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier` decides it, `dsh-tool-fs` dispatches inside `resolveRegularReadTarget` before `stat` so a denial never reveals presence.
6. New `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED`; the model sees verbatim `read denied: "<path>" is validator-owned — it is not part of this task; continue without it`, with no recovery instruction because no retry succeeds.
7. `read-barrier/denied` logs `{ version, role, capability, displayPath, root }` (`ignorable: true`); the path is already in the model's own `tool/call` args, so it adds evidence and no disclosure.
8. `ToolDefinition` gains never-model-visible `authority?: readonly ToolAuthority[]` with `session-log` / `plugin-mount` / `runtime-introspection`; `tool-session-query` and `tool-cordis` declare theirs, so a later log-reading tool is covered by its own declaration rather than a name list.
9. `preset.yml` gains `role`; `validator` is refused from a `user`-trust preset (the roster's first enforcing use of `trust`); `mountPreset` audits the settled subtree beside `inactiveRows` and a rejected mount rolls the whole session creation back.
10. A per-agent `ctx.tools.guard()` covers tools registered into the agent's own layer after mount, with exact refusal text pinned for both the mount and the guard.
11. `process` isolation is real: `SandboxPolicy`/`SandboxExecutionPolicy` gain `deniedReadRoots`, filled by `sandbox-policy` from the barrier, implemented per `sandbox-local` backend, `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` when a backend cannot express it; `tool-fs-search` confines its ripgrep spawn; workflow workers and out-of-process subagent providers refuse to start.
12. Certificate invariant: `recordRun()` and `./invariant` refuse a claim above the recorded `enforcement` (`VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN`) and refuse any certificate whose `read-barrier/scope` census carries a denied authority; the census is cross-checked against each `request/header`'s tool names.
13. `host` needs a `read-barrier/attestation` event the barrier wrote after verifying a file owned by another uid, unwritable by the harness uid, containing the run's environment content hashes — a fact no in-process component can produce.
14. Tamper: check-owned paths = denied directories ∪ `task.immutable`; the runner records the digest post-overlay and per attempt, `verification/run` gains `verdict: 'pass'|'fail'|'tampered'`, `foldTrajectory` gains basis `tamper` with `outcome: 0` outranking any certificate.
15. Blind judge under one licence: fresh `SessionId`, no `parentSessionId`, no resume/fork seed, `meta.cwd` a copy at the audited `treeHash`, derived history exactly judge prompt + task prompt + one evidence message, `system`-trust preset declaring `role: validator`, `judge/session` event asserting empty lineage.

Rollout is seven slices (barrier → fs denial → authority/guard → certificate invariant → process enforcement → tamper → judge), each independently green; fixtures named `read-barrier/`, `read-barrier-guard/`, `read-barrier-tamper/` under `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/`, snapshots `read-barrier-denied/` and `read-barrier-tamper/` under `.../tests/snapshots/`.

### Open questions I could not settle from the repository

- **`2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md` does not exist** anywhere in the repo or its refs, yet `docs/subsystems/improvement.{md,zh.md}`, `packages/improvement/fleet/README.{md,zh.md}` and `packages/improvement/fleet/src/index.ts` already link to it — so I could not cite P4's parent note. I linked the seams note for the rationale instead; when the sibling lands this note should gain a link to it.
- **`verification/run` and per-attempt `treeHash` do not exist yet** — only the environment-runner and fleet READMEs promise them. I specified the `verdict` field this note adds but could not confirm the payload it extends.
- **Enforcing on `trust`** contradicts `dsh-agent-presets`' README ("the `trust` field exists so consumers can present that difference, not to enforce it"). I proposed the amendment explicitly; the roster's owner may prefer a separate config naming which roots may declare `validator`.
- **Windows `host` attestation**: I leaned on `dsh-sandbox-windows-acl` for the ownership/write test without auditing whether it exports a read-only ACL query.
- **Landlock partial enforcement**: whether the per-platform launcher can express read denial when `SandboxEnforcement` is `partial`. I specified `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` as the fail-closed answer without reading the rule-building code.
- **Package group placement**: `dsh-read-barrier` in `packages/verification/` (subject is the validator root) versus `packages/sandbox/` beside `sandbox-policy` (shape is per-session confinement policy). I chose the former and stated it.
- **`glob`/`grep` at `isolation: none`** still descend into the barrier root when rooted above it. Recorded as an accepted `none`-level leak rather than adding a ripgrep exclusion I could not prove complete.
- The note names `subagent-claude-code` and `subagent-codex` — existing repository package identifiers the implementer must refuse, not model identifiers. Flagging in case you read the constraint more strictly.
